detailed_description: The QR Generator creates a PNG QR code from text or a URL entered on the page. It uses the bundled QR code library with a fixed 300 pixel output, margin, black foreground, and white background. The preview updates from the current input and can be downloaded as qrcode.png. This is useful for quick links, short text, testing scan behavior, or adding a simple QR code to notes and drafts. For print-critical work, test the downloaded image with the scanner and physical size you plan to use.
usage_steps: Enter the URL or text you want to encode.
Click Generate QR or let the preview update from the current input.
Check the QR preview in the page.
Scan the preview with a phone or test device.
Click Download PNG when the code scans correctly.
Use a clear quiet area around the QR code in final designs.
usage_examples: Create a QR code for a landing page URL.
Generate a QR code for a short Wi-Fi instruction note.
Download a PNG QR code for a presentation slide.
Test whether a long URL still scans reliably before sharing.

faqs.question: What can I put into the QR code?
faqs.answer: You can enter text or a URL. Shorter content usually scans more easily.

faqs.question: What file format can I download?
faqs.answer: The page downloads the generated QR code as a PNG file.

faqs.question: Can I customize the QR colors on this page?
faqs.answer: The current implementation uses a black foreground and white background.

faqs.question: How large is the generated QR preview?
faqs.answer: The current preview is generated at 300 pixels wide.

faqs.question: Should I test the QR code before printing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Always scan the downloaded QR code at the intended size and distance before using it in print or signage.
